blocking_issues.issue: The denied-cast flash reverts the fill Image to a hardcoded `normalColor` field defaulting to Color.white, rather than capturing the fill Image's actual pre-existing color. The production scene (Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity, fill Image fileID 935315373) has m_Color set to blue (r:0,g:0,b:1,a:1), not white. Because this candidate does not (and per the task's execution_reason, is not expected to) modify the scene, the new `normalColor`/`deniedColor` serialized fields on the existing scene-wired PlayerManaUI component will deserialize to their C# field-initializer defaults (white/red) rather than any scene-authored value. The first denied-cast flash will therefore permanently recolor the previously-blue, continuously-visible mana indicator to white, a real visual regression of the existing 'continuous mana indicator' behavior recorded in repository_evidence_at_bootstrap. This is masked by the added Play Mode tests because they construct a fresh Image via AddComponent<Image>(), whose default color (white) happens to match the new field's hardcoded default, so the tests cannot catch the scene-color mismatch.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Cache the fill Image's actual color at startup (e.g. in Awake/OnEnable, `normalColor = fillImage.color` when not deliberately overridden) instead of relying on a hardcoded Color.white default, so the denied-flash revert restores whatever color the scene/artist configured, or explicitly update the scene's PlayerManaUI serialized fields to match the existing blue tint.

criteria_results.evidence: PlayerMana.cs adds `public void ResetMana() { CurrentMana = maxMana; timeSinceLastSpend = postCastRegenDelay; }`, restoring current mana to full and setting the post-cast regen-delay timer to the same 'no pending delay' state Awake() establishes, matching GDD §5's owner-controlled reset interface and GDD §2 Loss/Restart's requirement that Player Mana and its regen-delay state be reset participants.

PlayerMana.cs adds `public event Action<float> CastDenied;` invoked only in Spend() when `amount > CurrentMana` (the insufficient-mana refusal branch), and not for the amount<=0 branch or the successful-spend branch (which raises ManaSpent instead), satisfying the requirement for a signal distinct from a successful spend.

The patch adds only ResetMana(), CastDenied, and the internal branching in Spend(); no Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave cooldown, charge, cast, placement, or active-field state was introduced into PlayerMana.cs. The new PlayerMana_PublicApiSurface_OnlyOwnsManaAndRegenDelayState test locks the public member set to CurrentMana/MaxMana/PostCastRegenDelay/ManaSpent/CastDenied/ResetMana/Spend/Tick.

PlayerManaPlayModeTests.cs was extended with ResetMana and CastDenied coverage (ResetMana_RestoresCurrentManaToFull_AfterPartialSpend, ResetMana_RestoresCurrentManaToFull_AfterManaFullySpent, ResetMana_ClearsPostCastRegenDelayTimerState, Spend_RaisesCastDenied_WhenAmountExceedsCurrentMana, Spend_DoesNotRaiseCastDenied_WhenSpendSucceeds, and regression tests) while the original Spend/regen/post-cast-delay tests are untouched. No Unity Test Runner execution occurred, so 'continues to pass' is unverified from source review alone.

PlayerManaUI_FlashesDeniedColor_OnCastDenied_ThenRevertsAfterDuration was added asserting a color flash on denied casts, but this requires actual Play Mode execution to validate readability, which was not run; additionally the flash-revert logic has a source-provable defect (see blocking issue) that undermines confidence the readable feedback matches the production-configured mana indicator.

The same PlayerManaUI test targets the existing fill Image mana indicator per GDD §3, but requires Unity Play Mode execution and human visual confirmation per the test author's own proposed_unity_test_scope, neither of which occurred; the scene-color mismatch defect further undercuts the fidelity of what was tested versus the real scene.

risks: The reflection-based tests (private field access on PlayerMana.timeSinceLastSpend and PlayerManaUI's mana/fillImage/normalColor/deniedColor/deniedFlashDuration) are brittle to field renames, matching an existing project pattern but increasing coupling between tests and private implementation details.
None of the added or existing tests were actually executed (no Unity Test Runner run occurred), so compilation success and pass/fail status for VAL-001/VAL-002/VAL-003 remain unverified.

The PlayerManaUI color-flash regression (see blocking issue) would not surface in CI because the added tests construct isolated GameObjects with default-white Images rather than exercising the actual scene-wired component.
structured_output.summary: AC-001, AC-002, and AC-003 are correctly satisfied at the source level: ResetMana() restores CurrentMana to maxMana and resets timeSinceLastSpend to postCastRegenDelay (mirroring Awake's cleared-timer state), CastDenied fires only on the insufficient-mana refusal path distinct from ManaSpent, and no spell-local state was added to PlayerMana's public surface. However, the PlayerManaUI denied-cast flash implementation has a genuine, source-provable regression: it reverts to a hardcoded Color.white default rather than the scene's actual blue-configured fill Image color, which will silently discolor the production mana indicator after the first denied cast — a defect the added tests cannot catch because they use fresh, default-colored Image objects. VAL-001/VAL-002/VAL-003 require Unity Play Mode execution that was not performed and remain not_proven.
